sourceFinding.quotedEvidence: prisma/schema.prisma's DebtEvent.sourceLedgerEntryId (the invariant's own named example field) is, confirmed by grep across the entire lib/ and app/ trees this session, NEVER WRITTEN anywhere in production code -- only read (lib/financial-core-db/adapter.ts:194, with a `?? undefined` fallback for the always-null case).

task: Determine whether invariant 35's guarantee for the sourceLedgerEntryId example is REQUIRED_NOW_AND_IMPLEMENTED (some real app/ code path today creates a DebtEvent from a ledger-derived source and needs the link) or DEFERRED_TO_A_NAMED_FUTURE_PHASE_BY_ARCHITECTURE_DECISION (no current caller needs it; the field genuinely belongs to future reconciliation work). Explicitly forbidden: writing a fake/placeholder value into sourceLedgerEntryId merely to make the check pass.

documentsRead: docs/HEADROOM-ARCHITECTURE-INVARIANTS.md (invariant 35's exact text, and the Phase 3-7 stable-sequence definition at the end of the document)

docs/HEADROOM-ROADMAP.md (in full; specifically the FinancialSnapshot/FinancialState fork discussion, the LedgerEntry/DebtEvent fork discussion at line 178 of the current document, and the Phase 5/Phase 6 goal statements)
codeRead: prisma/schema.prisma — DebtEvent model (id, companyId, facilityId, eventType, date, amount, refinancesFacilityId, relatedPermissionIds, sourceLedgerEntryId, provenance) and LedgerEntry model (id, companyId, documentId, date, description, basket, amount, direction, source) — two structurally separate models with no foreign-key relation between them; sourceLedgerEntryId is a bare nullable String, not a Prisma relation field

lib/financial-core-db/adapter.ts — loadDebtEvents() (the sole reader of sourceLedgerEntryId, line ~194, `sourceLedgerEntryId: r.sourceLedgerEntryId ?? undefined`); no writer of debtEvent rows anywhere in lib/ or app/

lib/financial-core/* (capital-structure.ts, liquidity.ts, position-service.ts, maturity.ts, interest.ts, scenario.ts, scenario-service.ts, solver-adapter.ts, types.ts) — all pure, in-memory functions that consume DebtEvent[] already loaded from the DB; none construct or persist a new DebtEvent

app/[companyId]/ledger/actions.ts — addLedgerEntry(), deleteLedgerEntry(), commitRestrictedPayment() — the live, real LedgerEntry write paths (manual entry and the Simulate tab's 'commit to ledger' action). None of these create or touch a DebtEvent row.

app/[companyId]/feeds/actions.ts — the FeedQueue LEDGER_ENTRY-kind approval path, another live LedgerEntry write path (from an approved connector/feed item). Also does not create or touch a DebtEvent row.

scripts/populate-coherent-financial-core.ts, scripts/populate-matthews-financial-provenance.ts, scripts/financial-core-acceptance-run.ts — the only three places in the entire repository that call `prisma.debtEvent.create`/`createMany`. All three are one-off, offline, engineer-run data-population/acceptance scripts that hand-type DebtEvent rows directly from primary sources (SEC filings, 8-Ks) with a ProvencancedFact provenance wrapper. None of them read from, or link to, any LedgerEntry row when constructing a DebtEvent — there is no LedgerEntry row in the current data model that a DebtEvent script-created row could accurately be said to originate from.
greps: grep -rn "DebtEvent" lib app prisma scripts — enumerated every reference; confirmed all `debtEvent.create`/`createMany` call sites live in scripts/, none in app/ or lib/

grep -rn "prisma\.ledgerEntry" lib app prisma scripts — confirmed LedgerEntry IS created by live app/ code (app/[companyId]/ledger/actions.ts, app/[companyId]/feeds/actions.ts, and prisma/seed.ts), unlike DebtEvent

grep -rn "sourceLedgerEntryId" . — exactly 4 hits total: the schema field declaration, the DebtEvent TypeScript type, the DB row interface, and the single read-with-fallback site in adapter.ts. Zero write sites anywhere.
keyFindings: No live app/ route creates a DebtEvent at all, today, under any circumstance. Every DebtEvent row that exists in any environment was put there by an engineer running an offline script.

LedgerEntry, by contrast, IS created live today, but only for a narrow, unrelated purpose: restricted-payment-pool (dividend/investment/asset-sale/debt-incur/debt-repay/equity) basket usage tracking for the legacy covenant engine. This matches docs/HEADROOM-ROADMAP.md's own characterization: 'LedgerEntry is real and load-bearing... but narrow — a flat 6-value basket enum, not a rich transaction record.'

DebtEvent and LedgerEntry are not two views of the same underlying event stream today — they are populated by entirely disjoint mechanisms (offline scripts vs. live UI/feed actions) recording different things (facility-level issuance/repayment/refinancing history vs. RP-pool basket usage). There is currently no real-world case where creating one should, today, populate a reference to the other, because the offline DebtEvent-population scripts are not derived from LedgerEntry rows in the first place — they are derived from primary filings.

docs/HEADROOM-ROADMAP.md is explicit and unambiguous that this exact fork is future work, by name: 'DebtEvent is the richer, newer, event-sourced model, explicitly designed with a sourceLedgerEntryId link back to LedgerEntry that has never actually been populated. Migration path: Phase 6 is where these should be reconciled into the real transaction/capacity-truth ledger described in North Star §2C.' The Phase 6 section header itself repeats this: 'This is also where the current LedgerEntry/DebtEvent fork (§3.3) gets resolved into the real transaction/capacity-truth model.'

The roadmap's stable phase sequence (also restated verbatim in docs/HEADROOM-ARCHITECTURE-INVARIANTS.md's closing ARCHITECTURE_CHANGE_PROPOSAL section) names Phase 5 as 'Financial Data / Continuous Monitoring' (canonical ontology reconciliation of FinancialSnapshot/FinancialState, connector framework, ERP/treasury connections, AI-assisted mapping, reconciliation/approval, sync/freshness) and Phase 6 as 'Living Headroom State' (the real unified dependency graph, living basket ledger, incremental recomputation). The LedgerEntry/DebtEvent reconciliation is named specifically under Phase 6, not Phase 5 — Phase 5's scope is the FinancialSnapshot/FinancialState fork, a different, adjacent fork the roadmap is careful to distinguish from the LedgerEntry/DebtEvent one.

Writing any value into sourceLedgerEntryId today — even a 'best effort' heuristic match against an existing LedgerEntry row — would be fabricated provenance: there is no real, current causal relationship between a script-populated DebtEvent (sourced from an 8-K) and any LedgerEntry row (sourced from manual RP-pool entry or a feed approval) to honestly record. Doing so would trade a disclosed, honest gap (invariant 35, correctly flagged VIOLATED) for a dishonest one (fabricated provenance, violating invariants 1, 2, and 4), which is explicitly forbidden by this workstream's charter and by the invariants document's own provenance rules.

conclusion.reasoning: No current app/ code path creates a DebtEvent, ledger-derived or otherwise; the only DebtEvent writers in the entire codebase are offline, engineer-run, one-off data-population scripts that source their data directly from primary filings, with no LedgerEntry counterpart to link to. LedgerEntry is a live but narrow, purpose-unrelated model (legacy RP-pool basket tracking). The two logs are not currently reconcilable in any factually honest way because they do not currently record overlapping events for the same company transaction — the reconciliation invariant 35 demands presupposes a real transaction/capacity-truth model that unifies them, which docs/HEADROOM-ROADMAP.md explicitly, by name, assigns to Phase 6 ('Living Headroom State'), not to any phase already built or in progress. Implementing sourceLedgerEntryId population now, absent that unified model, would require fabricating a link that does not exist, which this workstream's charter explicitly forbids and which would itself violate invariants 1/2/4 (provenance may never be fabricated). Therefore this is a genuine, evidence-based architecture-scope finding, not an excuse to skip a fixable gap: the field is real, currently and correctly unpopulated, and the invariant's own text already discloses this must not be worked around with a placeholder.
conclusion.whatThisDoesNotClaim: This does NOT dispute or soften the original certification finding that sourceLedgerEntryId is never written in production code today — that finding is factually correct and remains true after this workstream's changes. What this resolves is the *scope and timing* of when invariant 35 requires that field to be written: not now, because no current code path has a real, honest link to write, but at Phase 6, when the LedgerEntry/DebtEvent fork is architecturally reconciled per the roadmap's own explicit plan. The general principle of invariant 35 (no schema field may exist for a reconciliation purpose while permanently and silently going unpopulated with no plan to ever populate it) is fully preserved and is exactly why a named target phase, not silence, is required here.
